title: Hellenic DPA fines Teleperformance Greece EUR 100 000 under GDPR over a former employee's access request
date_note: EDPB published the news on 25 November 2026; the page lists the HDPA's final decision date as 05/10/2026.
geo_basis: country, as the source gives no city
summary: The EDPB page says the Hellenic Data Protection Authority imposed two fines on Teleperformance Greece, EUR 60 000 and EUR 40 000, a total of EUR 100 000. The case began with a former employee's complaint about an access request. The authority found the company did not provide a complete copy of his data, erased data before his employment ended despite pending legal claims, and lacked adequate security measures and request-handling procedures.
plain: Greece's data regulator fined Teleperformance Greece EUR 100 000 after a former employee's data access request was mishandled and his data was erased too early.
exec: A regulator fined a company EUR 100 000 for how it handled a data access request and for lacking measures to prevent data erasure.
impact: Two fines: EUR 60 000 and EUR 40 000, a total of EUR 100 000.

evidence.quote: (i) a fine of EUR 60 000 for infringements of Articles 5(1)(a) and (f), 15 and 17(3)(e) of the GDPR,
(ii) a fine of EUR 40 000 for infringements of Articles 5(2), 12(3), 13 and 32 of the GDPR,
amounting to a total of EUR 100 000.

validation.note: Single page, the EDPB's own news item relaying the Hellenic DPA decision; the decision itself was not read.
